topic: Source-forest complete observational fibers for strict Poisson branching SCMs. For every finite labeled causally sufficient DAG with independent positive Poisson innovations and edge-specific independent Bernoulli thinning probabilities strictly between zero and one, characterize the unrestricted observational fiber D(P). Prove that singleton/pair and degree-four log-PGF coefficient signatures fix the skeleton and every arrow entering a multi-parent vertex; after deleting those arrows the residual graph is a forest whose anchored components have forced roots and whose free components may be independently rerooted, and prove these are all and only the compatible DAGs. Give the explicit positive source-edge reversal preserving the complete PGF, the exact fiber cardinality, compelled-edge certificates, and the reverse-topological rational decoder yielding the unique parameter point on each compatible DAG. Prove degree-four coefficients determine the entire strict-model law and fiber and are sharp because strict triangle laws can agree through degree three while differing at the squared-sink monomial. From bounded count-cell indicators construct a simultaneous low-degree coefficient confidence region, outward-invert it to a graph set covering the full unrestricted fiber, and report only arrows unanimous over the nonempty outer set; do not claim automatic faithfulness or unrestricted uniform singleton recovery. Consumer: the football-event and shopping-mall PB-SCM analyses of Xiang et al. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fresh presolver derived the fixed-DAG inverse, complete-PGF source-reversal identity, residual-forest converse, and degree-four triangle lower bound. Exact rational checks recovered the correct fibers for every 2-, 3-, and 4-node DAG, tested all eligible source reversals through four nodes, and reproduced 29,281 five-node DAGs in 13,521 source-forest classes; diamonds, linked multi-parent vertices, overlapping descendants, and a complete five-node graph produced no counterexample. It also derived degree-four log-PGF coefficients as finite rational functions of bounded count-cell probabilities and a Hoeffding-union confidence region. Boundary thinning probabilities, zero innovation rates, automatic faithfulness, generic CAD as the headline, unrestricted singleton consistency, and a compact-box target substitution were tested and excluded. Focused current/citing searches found local PGF/cumulant rules and a latent-confounded three-variable extension, but no global source-forest converse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Formalize the arbitrary-DAG genealogy-to-coefficient lemma when multiple downstream paths repeat vertex labels, then connect it rigorously to every local signature used by the forest converse. EARLY KILL TEST: On a six-node rational graph with a reversible source edge, overlapping descendants, a downstream collider, and an anchored tail, enumerate every skeleton orientation and compare its exact full-PGF decoder with the predicted forest family; any missing representation, false positive, nonunique parameter point, or failed reversal stops the claim. open_problems.open_problem: What is the complete observational fiber of a strict causally sufficient Poisson branching SCM, including exactly which arrows are compelled, which source-edge reversals preserve the law, and how many compatible labeled DAGs and parameter points each law has?

source_refs.claim: PB-SCM causal pairs can be distributionally equivalent, while the paper gives only sufficient path-based conditions for orienting particular pairs.
source_refs.author: Jie Qiao, Yu Xiang, Zhengming Chen, Ruichu Cai, and Zhifeng Hao

source_refs.claim: The PGF paper identifies the skeleton and several local structures, but does not characterize every globally observationally equivalent DAG.
source_refs.author: Yu Xiang, Jie Qiao, Zhefeng Liang, Zihuai Zeng, Ruichu Cai, and Zhifeng Hao

source_refs.claim: The paper describes the Poisson-innovation PB-SCM DAG as generally only partially identifiable and obtains full identification by changing the thinning or innovation model.
source_refs.author: Penggang Gao, Ming Cai, and Hisayuki Hara

open_problems.why_unsolved: Available PB-SCM results stop at pairwise path criteria or sufficient local PGF signatures. Xiang et al.'s faithfulness-based skeleton-first reconstruction does not answer the unrestricted model-theoretic question of all DAGs generating one fixed law, while Gao et al. bypass the fiber by imposing different thinning or non-Poisson nonsink innovations. Focused searches found no arbitrary-DAG converse. The global obstacle is proving that overlapping descendant paths and repeated vertex labels in source genealogies create no equivalences beyond independently rerooting residual tree components, while also proving every permitted rerooting has a positive parameter transformation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient graph characterization of D(P), an explicit positive law-preserving source-edge reversal and exact cardinality formula, compelled-edge certificates, and a rational inverse proving a unique parameter point on every compatible DAG.

writing_exemplar.why: Its count-event motivation, transition from ordinary Markov equivalence to branching-specific asymmetry, and PGF-centered formulation are the closest framing to extend.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real event counts exhibit branching structure -> binomial thinning with Poisson innovations yields a tractable PB-SCM PGF -> local PGF signatures orient more edges than conditional independence -> the remaining problem is the complete global observational fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the recursive closed-form source PGF and its monomial-to-local-structure argument, replacing isolated local tests with a global genealogy decomposition and converse.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired fiber is defined by equality of the same PB-SCM PGF; the paper supplies the load-bearing representation but not the global equivalence classification.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the separation between distribution equivalence and conditional-independence equivalence, together with explicit transformations between law-equivalent graph representations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the structurally analogous problem of classifying directed graphs by generated distributions, although its algebra is linear Gaussian rather than Poisson-PGF.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over inversion over a discrete causal-model space and the proof that simultaneous nonrejection yields coverage for graph-derived relations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once D(P) is characterized, the estimation rung must cover a set of observationally compatible graphs and report relations shared across that set.

open_problems.open_problem: Is equality of the singleton, pair, and total-degree-at-most-four coefficients of the log-PGF sufficient to determine the entire strict PB-SCM law and observational fiber, and is degree four minimal?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives the recursive PGF and detects local structures through its components, without a finite universal truncation theorem or minimal-degree result.
source_refs.author: Yu Xiang, Jie Qiao, Zhefeng Liang, Zihuai Zeng, Ruichu Cai, and Zhifeng Hao

source_refs.claim: The paper connects arbitrary-order joint cumulants to directed paths and uses a discriminating order k rather than establishing a graph-independent cutoff.
source_refs.author: Jie Qiao, Yu Xiang, Zhengming Chen, Ruichu Cai, and Zhifeng Hao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Qiao et al.'s k-path cumulant decomposition allows the discriminating order to depend on path multiplicity, while Xiang et al.'s recursive PGF contains monomials of unbounded total degree on large DAGs. Degree-four completeness therefore requires a new compression argument: aggregate branching genealogies traversing several downstream paths and repeating observed vertex labels, then prove that their low-degree aggregates recover every local signature needed by a global fiber converse. Searches combining PB-SCM with finite truncation, degree-four coefficients, low-degree completeness, and sharpness found no occupied target-method pair. Minimality additionally requires two strict triangle parameterizations agreeing through degree three but separated at degree four.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if finite-signature characterization equating degree-at-most-four log-PGF agreement with equality of the full strict-model law and fiber, together with an explicit strict triangle counterexample proving failure at degree three.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative makes high-order information concrete through branching paths and asks which cumulant signatures distinguish directions, naturally setting up a universal low-order cutoff.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Count branching creates observationally symmetric causal pairs -> multiple directed paths leave higher-order cumulant signatures -> path signatures orient some edges -> determine whether one fixed low degree captures every required signature and whether that degree is sharp.

method_exemplars.technique: Use structural recursion for the complete PGF and the correspondence between log-PGF monomials and branching structures, then quotient genealogies by repeated vertex labels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target coefficients belong to the same recursive log-PGF; the missing step is showing that a bounded subset determines every graph-relevant component.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the joint-cumulant decomposition into path contributions and its forward-versus-reverse asymmetry argument to isolate the first degree at which a local orientation becomes visible.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed degree-three lower bound and degree-four witness are finite-order versions of the paper's path-multiplicity asymmetry.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over empirical-PGF estimation and its limit-theory reasoning, specialized to finitely many multivariate coefficient functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A universal finite signature turns PB-SCM recovery into inference on a fixed collection of PGF functionals rather than estimation of the full count distribution.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a simultaneous finite-sample confidence set for the full unrestricted strict PB-SCM observational fiber from bounded count-cell indicators, with compelled arrows reported only when unanimous over a nonempty outward-inverted graph set?

source_refs.claim: The paper estimates PGF-based statistics by bootstrap and identifies scalable, sample-efficient estimation as an open direction.
source_refs.author: Yu Xiang, Jie Qiao, Zhefeng Liang, Zihuai Zeng, Ruichu Cai, and Zhifeng Hao

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that graph-then-inference can undercover and develops test inversion accounting for structural uncertainty in restricted linear causal models.
source_refs.author: David Strieder, Tobias Freidling, Stefan Haffner, and Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs asymptotically valid ordering sets for additive-error SEMs, not finite-sample PB-SCM sets covering a non-singleton population fiber.
source_refs.author: Y. Samuel Wang, Mladen Kolar, and Mathias Drton
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Xiang et al.'s practical procedure thresholds bootstrap statistics and outputs a learned graph; it neither targets the full non-singleton fiber nor provides simultaneous coverage for every structural conclusion. Existing causal-discovery confidence-set papers use test inversion in linear or additive-error models, generally asymptotically, and do not exploit bounded indicators for discrete count cells. The first proof step that changes is to express all required low-degree log-PGF coefficients as rational functions of finitely many bounded cell probabilities, control their denominators and coordinates on one joint event, and propagate that event through a set-valued outward inverse rather than a discontinuous point decoder. Focused searches found no PB-SCM construction of this kind.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample 1-alpha coefficient region and outward-inversion procedure whose graph set contains every DAG in D(P) with probability at least 1-alpha, plus a simultaneous coverage theorem for arrows unanimous over the nonempty outer set.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames causal-discovery uncertainty around the structures the data do not rule out and post-processes only relations shared across that set.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Identifiability results motivate point graph estimators -> finite samples leave several structures compatible with the data -> confidence sets prevent overconfident structural conclusions -> build a PB-SCM set covering the population fiber and report only unanimous arrows.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt model-space test inversion and its coverage proof retaining every structural model compatible with a joint acceptance event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired outer graph set must preserve uncertainty in graph structure and numerical parameters rather than condition on one selected PB-SCM DAG.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt confidence-set post-processing into lower and upper envelopes of causal relations, including explicit treatment of an empty set as model criticism.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Unanimous-arrow reporting over a nonempty PB-SCM outer set directly parallels reporting ancestral relations shared by all nonrejected causal orderings.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the empirical probability-generating function as an average of bounded transforms and specialize its inference construction to finitely many multivariate coefficient coordinates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies classical count-data PGF inference machinery; the new step replaces pointwise goodness-of-fit statistics with simultaneous bounded-functional control and outward inversion.

open_problems.open_problem: How does the complete observational fiber change in latent-confounded Poisson branching SCMs beyond the three-observed-variable patterns currently classified by monomial equivalence?

source_refs.claim: The LC-PB-SCM paper proves a Trie representation and a complete identifiability condition only for local three-variable patterns distinguishable up to monomial equivalence.
source_refs.author: Jie Qiao, Zihuai Zeng, Ruichu Cai, Zhengming Chen, and Zhifeng Hao

source_refs.claim: The causally sufficient PGF analysis supplies recursive local signatures but treats causal sufficiency as a restrictive modeling assumption.
source_refs.author: Yu Xiang, Jie Qiao, Zhefeng Liang, Zihuai Zeng, Ruichu Cai, and Zhifeng Hao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Qiao et al. enter the latent-confounded model but confine their completeness result to local triples. In a larger observed graph, latent innovations can generate overlapping descendant Tries whose monomials collide after hidden labels are marginalized, so the local classification does not automatically compose into a global fiber. The first proof step that changes from the causally sufficient source-genealogy argument is replacing one observed source per independent Poisson cluster with hidden-root Trie factors and determining when distinct hidden-root factorizations induce the same observed log-PGF. Searches for LC-PB-SCM global observational fibers or arbitrary-node completeness returned only the local three-variable result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization of all observed-DAG and latent-root representations inducing one LC-PB-SCM law, including identifiable observed arrows, admissible hidden-root Trie refactorizations, and uniqueness or multiplicity of positive parameters.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates latent confounding in event-count branching systems and formulates distinguishability through observed PGF monomials.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real branching-count systems contain hidden common causes -> causally sufficient PB-SCM signatures may then mislead -> Trie representations expose latent contributions to observed PGF monomials -> extend local triple completeness to the global observational fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize the Trie representation theorem and local monomial-equivalence case split to overlapping observed descendant sets and multiple hidden roots.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It introduces the exact latent PB-SCM algebra whose global factorization ambiguity must be characterized.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over recursive PGF localization and graph-signature extraction, replacing observed-source factors with marginalized hidden-root Trie factors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causally sufficient representation is the baseline recovered when no hidden factor contributes to multiple observed branches.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt inversion over candidate causal representations and envelope reporting so uncertainty over latent structures remains in observed ancestral conclusions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A non-singleton latent fiber requires set-valued inference and conclusions unanimous across nonrejected representations.

literature_map:
Steutel and van Harn (1979, Annals of Probability) established thinning and discrete self-decomposability algebra underlying binomial thinning.
Al-Osh and Alzaid (1987, Journal of Time Series Analysis) made binomial thinning with Poisson immigration the classical INAR(1) branching-count model.
Nakamura and Pérez-Abreu (1993, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics; Canadian Journal of Statistics) developed empirical-PGF methods for count inference.
Shimizu et al. (2006, JMLR) and Peters et al. (2014, JMLR) are foundational examples of structure identification through non-Gaussian or nonlinear SEM asymmetry.
Park and Raskutti (2015, NeurIPS; 2018, JMLR) identify conditional-Poisson DAGs through overdispersion, a different count SCM from inherited-event thinning.
Choi, Chapkin, and Ni (2020, NeurIPS) and Choi et al. (2023, JMLR) identify zero-inflated count DAGs through conditional distributional form rather than branching genealogies.
Ghassami et al. (2020, ICML) distinguish distribution equivalence from Markov equivalence and provide an adjacent template for full fiber analysis.
Qiao et al. (2024, AAAI) introduce PB-SCM path-cumulant identification, show bivariate reversal equivalence, and provide sufficient rather than complete orientation conditions.
Xiang et al. (2024, NeurIPS) derive the recursive PB-SCM PGF and local graph signatures but stop short of a global observational-fiber converse.
Xiang et al. also flag scalable, sample-efficient PGF estimation as open, while their bootstrap procedure does not cover the full structural fiber.
Strieder et al. (2021, UAI) demonstrate graph-then-inference undercoverage and introduce causal-model test inversion in restricted linear systems.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026, JASA; arXiv 2023) construct asymptotically valid causal-ordering sets and relation envelopes, but not finite-sample count-SCM fiber sets.
Qiao et al. (2026, ICML) extend PB-SCMs to latent confounding with a Trie theorem and complete local three-variable monomial-equivalence analysis; global completeness remains absent.
Gao, Cai, and Hara (2026, arXiv) call strict Poisson PB-SCMs generally partially identifiable and obtain full DAG identification by changing the thinning or nonsink innovation model.
Focused exact-phrase and citing searches found no source-forest global converse, universal sharp degree-four cutoff, or simultaneous honest coverage of the unrestricted PB-SCM fiber.
